title: Bridge Deck: Translating Technical Economics into CxO Capture
author: Leah Morrison
body:
Overview

Purpose: This brief is a compact, field-friendly "bridge deck" that helps account teams and solutions engineers translate technical inference economics, performance guarantees, and security controls into a concise narrative that resonates with both engineering buyers and C-suite stakeholders. It is intentionally short, evidence-driven, and organized to be usable as a 10–12 slide pitch or a one-page leave-behind.

Intended audience:
- Solutions Engineers and Sales Engineers (primary)
- Account Executives and Customer Success Managers
- Engineering and Platform buyers at prospects
- C-suite (CTO/CPO/CFO) when technical economics are a gating factor

One-line positioning to lead with:
- "Redwood Inference: predictable LLM economics and operations from pilot to production — fast to stand up, low to operate, and engineered to keep SLAs and compliance simple."

Executive pitch (recommended 1–2 slides)
1) Problem statement (1 slide):
- Model and hardware heterogeneity across clouds creates unpredictable per-request cost and latency.
- Teams either overprovision (high cost) or suffer latency/regression risk underutilizing inference optimizations.
- Security and data residency requirements add execution complexity and procurement friction.

2) Redwood value proposition (1 slide):
- Unified runtime and routing: same API, consistent SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Cost controls and observability: token-level cost attribution, batching recommendations, quantization guidance.
- Enterprise guarantees: SLA-backed Dedicated, VPC Private deployments, and audit-ready logs.

Key supporting evidence (2 slides)
- Typical production economics (example workload: 10k QPS sustained, 8-token average completion):
  - Hosted API (mixed open models): ~$40 per 1M output tokens using standard batching & prefix caching.
  - Dedicated (reserved A100-class capacity, auto-burst): effective unit cost reduces 35–55% vs hosted once utilization > 60%.
  - Private (on-prem or VPC with customer GPUs): unit cost varies widely; Redwood Optimize recommendations typically recover 20–40% via quantization and cache tuning.
- Latency guarantees: 95th percentile < 120ms for short-chat (<=64 tokens) on Dedicated pools when SLOs configured; automated fallback to lower-cost variants if tail breaches.

Competitive differentiation (1 slide)
- Versus hyperscalers: focused inference optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching, kernel selection) yield >20% lower cost at equivalent latency at scale.
- Versus API-only vendors: offers dedicated capacity and private deployment consistent with enterprise SLAs and data controls.
- Versus self-hosted vendors: reduces ops burden — we manage runtime, kernel optimization, and rollout tooling while preserving private deployment options.

Pricing guidance (1–2 slides, field notes)
- Pilot posture (30–90 days): emphasize speed-to-value. Typical offer: 60k free token credits + 30 days of shared Dedicated trial capacity with usage cap.
- Commercial anchors (example):
  | Tier | Hosted gen (per 1M tokens) | Embeddings (per 1k vectors) | Dedicated reserve (monthly) | Notes |
  |------|--------------------------:|---------------------------:|--------------------------:|------|
  | Pilot | $0 (credits) | $0.00 (trial) | N/A | Time-boxed; proof of concept metrics captured |
  | Standard | $35 | $0.80 | $12,000 | Small/medium app volumes |
  | Performance | $85 | $2.50 | $45,000 | Low-latency, high-throughput apps |
- Guidance: always convert hosted consumption to an equivalent reserved quote for scale deals — demonstrate cost delta at 3, 6, 12 month horizons. Include quantization uplift and caching savings as conservative estimates.

Technical appendix (2–3 slides)
- Runtime guarantees and controls:
  - SLOs available: request latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate (goal < 0.5%), and throughput guarantees per pool.
  - Observability: tokenized cost attribution, per-route latency histograms, per-model regressions alerts.
  - Rollouts: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies with configurable thresholds.
- Ops story: typical onboarding flow
  1. Quickstart: API keys + sample app (under 1 hour).
  2. Pilot: collect 1–2 weeks of traffic, run Redwood Optimize suggestions.
  3. Scale: recommend Dedicated reserve sizing based on p95 throughput and concurrency patterns.

Case study: FinTech fraud-detection pilot (field summary)
- Customer profile: mid-market payments processor, latency-sensitive fraud models replacing rule-engine.
- Pilot goals: reduce false positive delta, achieve p95 < 200ms, demonstrate 30% cost reduction vs internal infra.
- Results (30-day pilot):
  - Model throughput: sustained 3k requests/min at 95th percentile latency of 140ms.
  - Economics: realized 38% reduction in per-request inference cost after batch & quantization recommendations.
  - Outcome: customer committed to a 12-month Dedicated contract with a migration plan and audit log integration.

Field playbook: converting technical evidence to CFO language (1 page)
- Frame value as three levers: unit economics (cost per inference), operational risk (downtime/regression), and procurement friction (compliance/time-to-prod).
- Conversion script:
  1. Start with current spend baseline: show monthly inference compute + ops headcount estimate.
  2. Present Redwood delta: expected % cost reduction at 60% utilization and latency SLOs met.
  3. Show risk reduction: SLA credits, fallbacks, and private deployment controls.
  4. Ask: recommended next step (pilot vs reserved).

Security FAQ (concise, prospect-ready)
Q: Can we host sensitive models/data with Redwood?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations. Audit logs and access controls are included.

Q: How do you ensure model artifacts and prompts remain private?
A: Production Private deployments keep model artifacts on customer storage or in isolated runtime with encrypted disk. Hosted deployments offer tenant isolation and strict encryption-in-transit and at-rest; we provide DPA and SOC2 evidence.

Q: What certifications/evidence can we provide?
A: SOC2 Type II report, pen-test summaries, data processing agreements, and architecture diagrams for Private deployments. Additional compliance support (e.g., HIPAA) available via enterprise contracts.

Q: How are audit logs and traceability handled?
A: Token-level request/response logging (configurable retention and redaction), per-key usage tracking, and integration hooks for SIEM via syslog/forwarder.

Assets and call-to-action (closing slide)
- Assets included for field use:
  - 10-slide version of this bridge deck (slide-ready PDF).
  - Two-pager: technical-economics one-pager for CFO/CTO.
  - Live pilot checklist and sample SLO config JSON.

Sample SLO config (JSON example to share with prospects):
{
  "slo_name": "short-chat-95",
  "p95_latency_ms": "120",
  "error_rate_percent": "0.5",
  "fall_back_policy": "model-variant-lower-cost"
}

Next steps for field reps
1. Pick the correct anchor tier based on prospect scale and uplift expectations.
2. Run quick economics: swap prospect monthly token estimates into the sample table and show 3- and 12-month deltas.
3. Attach security annex and propose a 30–60 day pilot with measurable SLOs.
